title: This Bug Pulls 400 g When It Jumps. Fighter Pilots Black Out at 10

scenes.text: This bug jumps at 400 g. Pilots black out at 10.
The froghopper. A quarter inch long. It launches 28 inches straight up. 100 times its body length.
Like a six-foot man jumping 600 feet. Straight up.
It winds its back legs up like a catapult, locks them, then releases everything at once.
Cambridge filmed it at 2,000 frames a second. A flea manages a tenth of that.
scenes.keywords: high speed camera slow motion insect

scenes.text: 400 g. And it grows up in a blob of spit on a plant stem.

description:
The froghopper, or spittlebug, is the highest jumping insect on Earth. Only about a quarter of an inch long, it can leap 70 centimetres (28 inches) into the air, more than 100 times its own body length.
Cambridge zoologist Malcolm Burrows filmed it at 2,000 frames a second and found it accelerates at over 400 g, about ten times the acceleration of a flea. Fighter pilots struggle past about 10 g. Scaled up, it is like a six-foot person jumping 600 feet.
Which insect do you think is the most underrated athlete? Comment below.
first_comment: The froghopper takes off in about one thousandth of a second. The foam you see on plant stems in spring is where its young hide. Which animal would win a jumping contest?
